Et iterum ait: Tollatur, ut non videat gloriam Domini, et cum hee facta fuerint, elongabit, inquit, Deus homines, et derelicti multiplicabuntur in terra. Ipsi autem sunt de quibus ait propheta: e¢ derelicti multiplicabuntur in terra. Ecce venient filit tui quos emisisti, venient collecti ab Oriente usque ad Occidentem verbo illius sancti, gaudentes ea que a Deo tuo est claritate. Exuere Hierusalem habitum luctus et afflictionis tue, et induere decorem ejus que a Deo tuo est claritatis in awternum: circumdare amictum duplicem ejus que a Deo tuo est justitie, impone mitram super caput tuum glorie eterne. Deus enim demonstrabit ei quae sub colo est universe tuum fulgorem. Vocabitur namque nomen tuum ab ipso Deo in weternum, pax justitice et glorie colenti Deo. Surge Hierusalem, et sta in excelso, et circumspice ad Orientem, et vide collectos filios tuos a Solis ortu usque ad Occidentem verbo illius sancti, gaudentes ipsam Dei recordationem. Profecti sunt enim a@ pedites, dum adducerentur ab inimicis. Introducet illos Deus ad te portatus cum gloria tanquam thronus regni. Decrevit enim Deus ut humilietur omnis mons excelsus, et congeries eterne, et ut valles impleantur, ad redigendam planitiem terre, ut ambulet Israel tute Dei gloria. Umbracula autem intewuerunt syloc, et lignum boni odoris ipsi Israel pracepto Dei. Provibit enim Deus cum letitia lumine claritatis suc, cum misericordia et justitia, quae ab ipso est. 2. Heec autem talia universa non in superccelestibus possunt intelligi: Deus enim, ait, demonstrabit ei que sub caclo est, universe tuum fulgorem; sed in Regni temporibus, revocata terra a Christo, et reedificata Hierusalem, secundum characterem qui ssursum est Hierusalem, de qua ait propheta Esaias: Zece in manibus meis depinai muros tuos, et in conspectu meo es semper. Et Apostolus autem scribens ad Galatas similiter ait: J//a autem que surswm est Hierusalem libera est, que est mater omnium nostrum ; non ex cogitatione erratici AXonis dicens hoc, neque virtute aliqua, que abscessit Pleromate, et Prunico; sed de Hierusalem quee in manibus descripta est. Et ipsam descendentem in Apocalypsi vidit Johannes super terram, novam. Post enim Regni tempora, Vidi, inquit, thronum album magnum, et sedentem in eo, cujus a facie fugit terra et colum, et locus non est eis. Et illa jam quee sunt generalis resurrectionis et judicii exponit vidisse, dicens mortuos magnos et minores. Dedit, inquit, > mare mortuos quos in se habuit, et mors et infert dederunt mortuos quos apud se habuerunt: et libri adaperti sunt. Et audivi, inquit, vocem magnam de throno dicentem: Ecce tabernaculum Dei cum hominibus, et habitabit cum eis, et ipsi populi ejus erunt, et ipse Deus cum eis erit corum Deus. Et delebit omnem lacrymam ab oculis eorum, et mors non erit amplius, non luctus non clamor neque dolor ulterius erit, quia prima abierunt. Et Esaias autem hoe ipsum ait: Erit enim obveniet eis in cor; sed latitiam et exultationem invenient in ea. autem est quod ab Apostolo dictum est: Preterit enim habitus hujus mundi. Similiter autem et Dominus ait: Terra et celum transiet. ~His itaque preetereuntibus super terram, novam superiorem Hierusalem ait Domini discipulus Johannes dere, quemadmodum sponsam ornatam viro suo; et hoe esse tabernaculum Dei, in quo inhabitabit Deus cum hominibus, HujusHierusalem imago illa, que in priori terra Hierusalem, in qua Sjusti preemeditantur incorruptelam, et parantur in salutem, Et hujus tabernaculi typum accepit Moyses in monte: et nihil allegorisari potest, sed omnia firma et vera, et substantiam habentia, ad fruitionem hominum justorum a Deo facta. Quomodo enim vere Deus est, qui resuscitat hominem; sic et vere resurgit a mortuis, et non allegorice, quemadmodum per tanta ostendimus.* Et sicut vere resurgit, sic et vere praemeditabitur ineorruptelam, et augebitur, et vigebit in regni temporibus, ut fiat CapaX glorize Patris. Deinde omnibus renovatis, vere in civitate habitabit Dei. Diwit, enim inquit, sedens super thronum: Ecce nova facio omnia. Et dicit Dominus; Omnia scribe, quomodo tt sermones fideles, et veri sunt. Et divit mihi, Facta sunt. Et secundum rationem.
thought_title: The Resurrection and the New Jerusalem
pass_a_gloss: But if certain ones have attempted to allegorize these things of this kind, they will not be able to be found consonant with themselves in all things, and they will be convinced by the very words themselves, because when the cities of the nations have been deserted, and the houses, because they are not inhabited by men, and the earth has been left deserted; For behold, Isaiah says, the day of the Lord is coming, incurable and full of fury and wrath, to put the city on the earth to be deserted, and to destroy sinners from it. And again he says: Let him be taken away, so that he may not see the glory of the Lord, and when these things have been done, God will prolong, he says, the days of men, and those who have been left behind will be multiplied on the earth. And they will build houses, and they themselves will inhabit them, and they will plant vineyards, and they themselves will eat them. These things have been spoken without controversy concerning the resurrection of the just, which occurs after the coming of the Antichrist and the destruction of all the nations that exist under heaven, in which the just will reign on the earth, growing from the vision of the Lord, and through him they will become accustomed to taking the glory of God, and the unity of spiritual things in the kingdom they will take. And those whom he finds on the earth, waiting for him from heaven, and having endured tribulation, who have also escaped the hands of the wicked. These are the ones about whom the prophet says: And those who have been left behind will be multiplied on the earth. And as many as God has prepared from the believers for this, to be left behind on the earth, and to be under the Kingdom of the Saints, and to minister to this Jerusalem, and the kingdom in it, Jeremiah the prophet has signified, saying: Look around, he says, to the East, Jerusalem, and the joy that comes to you from God himself. Behold, your sons whom you have sent out will come, coming together from the East to the West by the word of that holy one, rejoicing in the things that are from your God, with clarity. Put off, Jerusalem, the garment of mourning and your affliction, and put on the adornment of that which is from your God, with clarity, forever. Encircle yourself with a double garment of that which is from your God, justice, and put a mitre on your head, of eternal glory. For God will show to her what is under the whole heaven, your splendor. For your name will be called by God himself, forever, peace, justice, and glory, worshiping God. Arise, Jerusalem, and stand on high, and look around to the East, and see your sons gathered from the rising of the sun to the West, by the word of that holy one, rejoicing in the remembrance of God. For they have gone out on foot, while they were being led by their enemies. God will introduce them to you, carried with glory, like a throne of the kingdom. For God has decreed that every high mountain will be humbled, and the eternal gatherings, and that the valleys will be filled, to reduce the earth to a plain, so that Israel may walk securely in the glory of God. And the trees have overshadowed the sycamores, and the wood of good odor, by the command of God, for Israel. For God will prohibit with joy, with the light of his clarity, with mercy and justice, which are from him. But all these things cannot be understood in the supercelestial things; for God, he says, will show to her what is under the heaven, your splendor; but in the times of the Kingdom, when the earth has been recalled by Christ, and Jerusalem has been rebuilt, according to the character that is above, Jerusalem, about which the prophet Isaiah says: Behold, I have depicted your walls in my hands, and you are always in my sight. And the Apostle, writing to the Galatians, says similarly: But the Jerusalem that is above is free, which is the mother of us all; not from the thought of the erratic Axe, saying this, nor by any virtue that has gone out from the Pleroma, and the Prunic; but from the Jerusalem that has been described in the hands. And John saw it descending upon the earth, new, in the Apocalypse. For after the times of the Kingdom, I saw, he says, a great white throne, and one sitting on it, from whose face the earth and the heaven fled, and there was no place for them. And he explains the things that are of the general resurrection and judgment, saying: The sea gave up the dead that it had, and death and hell gave up the dead that they had; and the books were opened. And the book of life was opened, and the dead were judged from the things that were written in the books, according to their works; and death and hell were cast into the lake of fire, the second death. This is what is called Gehenna, which the Lord said is eternal fire. And if anyone, he says, has not been found written in the book of life, he was cast into the lake of fire. And after these things, he says: I saw a new heaven and a new earth; for the first heaven and the first earth have passed away, and there is no longer any sea. And I saw the holy city, new Jerusalem, descending from heaven, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband. And I heard, he says, a great voice from the throne, saying: Behold, the tabernacle of God is with men, and he will dwell with them, and they will be his people, and God himself will be with them, their God. And he will wipe away every tear from their eyes, and there will be no more death, no more mourning, no more crying, no more pain, because the former things have passed away. And Isaiah says the same thing: For it will be a joy and an exultation in it. This is what has been said by the Apostle: For the fashion of this world has passed away. Similarly, the Lord says: The earth and the heaven will pass away. When these things have passed away, the Lord's disciple John says that the new and superior Jerusalem will be on the earth, as a bride adorned for her husband; and this is the tabernacle of God, in which God will dwell with men. And the image of this Jerusalem is that which is in the former earth, Jerusalem, in which the just are prepared for incorruption, and are prepared for salvation. And Moses received the type of this tabernacle on the mountain; and nothing can be allegorized, but all things are firm and true, and have substance, made by God for the enjoyment of just men. For just as God is truly, who raises man; so also he truly rises from the dead, and not allegorically, as we have shown through so many things. And just as he truly rises, so also he will truly be prepared for incorruption, and will be increased, and will flourish in the times of the kingdom, so that he may become the glory of the Father. Then, when all things have been renewed, he will truly dwell in the city of God. For he says, sitting on the throne: Behold, I make all things new. And the Lord says: Write all things, how my words are faithful and true. And he says to me: They have been made. And according to reason.

pass_b_english: If some try to allegorize these things, they will not be able to square their readings with themselves on every point; the very words will convict them. For when the cities of the nations have been deserted, the houses left empty because no one lives in them, and the earth abandoned, see what Isaiah says: "The day of the Lord is coming, incurable, full of fury and wrath, to make the land a desolation and to destroy its sinners from it" (Isaiah 13:9; Isaiah 13:19). And again he says: "Let him be taken away, so that he may not see the glory of the Lord." When these things have come to pass, God will prolong the days of men, and those left behind will multiply on the earth. They will build houses and inhabit them; they will plant vineyards and eat their fruit. These words were spoken without controversy about the resurrection of the just, which takes place after the coming of the Antichrist and the destruction of all the nations that exist under heaven. In that time the just will reign on the earth, growing from the vision of the Lord, and through him they will become accustomed to taking the glory of God; the unity of spiritual things they will take up in the kingdom. They are those whom the Lord finds on the earth, waiting for him from heaven, who have endured tribulation and escaped the hands of the wicked. These are the ones of whom the prophet says: "And those who have been left behind will multiply on the earth." As many believers as God has prepared for this—to be left on the earth and to serve under the Kingdom of the Saints, ministering to this Jerusalem and the kingdom in it—Jeremiah the prophet has signified, saying: "Look toward the East, Jerusalem, and see the joy that comes to you from God himself. Behold, your sons whom you sent away will come, gathered from East to West by the word of the Holy One, rejoicing in the glory that is from your God. Put off, Jerusalem, the garment of your mourning and affliction, and put on forever the beauty of the glory from your God. Wrap yourself in the double garment of righteousness from your God; set upon your head the mitre of eternal glory. For God will show to her all your splendor under heaven. Your name will be called by God forever: Peace of Righteousness and Glory of God's Worship. Arise, Jerusalem, stand on the height; look toward the East, and see your children gathered from the rising of the sun to its setting by the word of the Holy One, rejoicing in the remembrance of God. For they went out on foot, led away by enemies; but God will bring them back to you, carried in glory as on a royal throne. For God has decreed that every high mountain be humbled and the ancient hills brought low, that the valleys be filled to make the ground level, so that Israel may walk securely in the glory of God. The woods have shaded the sycamores, and the sweet-smelling wood, by God's command, for Israel. For God will lead them with joy, in the light of his glory, with mercy and righteousness that proceed from him.

But all these things cannot be understood as belonging to a super-celestial realm; for God says he will show to her what is under heaven, your splendor. Rather, they belong to the times of the Kingdom, when the earth has been recalled by Christ and Jerusalem rebuilt according to the pattern that is above—Jerusalem about which the prophet Isaiah says: "Behold, I have engraved your walls on my palms; you are continually before me." And the Apostle, writing to the Galatians, says the same: "But the Jerusalem above is free, and she is our mother" (Galatians 4:26)—not from the fantasy of an erratic Aeon, nor by any virtue that flowed out of the Pleroma and the Prunicus, but from the Jerusalem that is described in the hands of God. And John saw her descending upon the earth, new, in the Apocalypse. For after the times of the Kingdom, he says: "I saw a great white throne and him who sat on it; from his face earth and heaven fled away, and no place was found for them" (Revelation 20:11). And he describes the things of the general resurrection and judgment: "The sea gave up the dead that were in it, Death and Hades gave up the dead that were in them, and the books were opened. The book of life was opened, and the dead were judged by what was written in the books, according to their deeds. Death and Hades were thrown into the lake of fire, the second death" (Revelation 20:12-14). This is what is called Gehenna, which the Lord called eternal fire. "And if anyone's name was not found written in the book of life, he was thrown into the lake of fire" (Revelation 20:15). After these things he says: "I saw a new heaven and a new earth, for the first heaven and the first earth had passed away, and the sea was no more. And I saw the holy city, new Jerusalem, coming down out of heaven from God, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband. And I heard a loud voice from the throne saying: 'Behold, the dwelling of God is with men; he will dwell with them, and they will be his people, and God himself will be with them as their God. He will wipe away every tear from their eyes, and death shall be no more, neither shall there be mourning, nor crying, nor pain anymore, for the former things have passed away'" (Revelation 21:1-4). And Isaiah says the same: "They shall obtain joy and gladness." This is what the Apostle said: "The fashion of this world is passing away." Likewise the Lord says: "Heaven and earth will pass away." When these things have passed away, the Lord's disciple John says that the new and higher Jerusalem will be on the earth, as a bride adorned for her husband; and this is the tabernacle of God in which God will dwell with men. The image of this Jerusalem is the Jerusalem that existed on the former earth, in which the just are prepared for incorruption and made ready for salvation. Moses received the type of this tabernacle on the mountain; and nothing can be allegorized, but all things are firm, true, and substantial, made by God for the enjoyment of the just. For just as God truly raises man, so he truly rose from the dead, not allegorically, as we have shown through so many proofs. And just as he truly rose, so he will truly be prepared for incorruption, and will increase and flourish in the times of the kingdom, that he may become capable of the glory of the Father. Then, when all things have been renewed, he will truly dwell in the city of God. For he who sits on the throne says: "Behold, I make all things new." And the Lord says: "Write this down, for these words are trustworthy and true." And he said to me: "It is done." And this accords with reason.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Latin text, including the complex theological arguments regarding the physical reality of the resurrection versus allegorical interpretation. All scripture citations in Pass B (Isaiah 13:9, 13:19, Galatians 4:26, Revelation 20:11-15, Revelation 21:1-4) correctly identify the quoted or alluded to content in the Latin source. The distinction between the 'supercelestial' and the earthly kingdom is preserved. OCR debris in the Latin (e.g., 'e¢', 'wdificabunt', 'ccelis', 'ssursum') was handled correctly by the translator.
